clue.text: Put down rook and leave pawn in discomfort

blocks.note: to put something down is to write it
R is the chess notation for a rook
scram is a slangy command to leave at once
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player finds an awkward position uncomfortable after giving up a rook and a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess words make the clue look like a game report, but rook and pawn are only there for their one-letter notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Writer's cramp is the aching hand muscle spasm brought on by long spells of penmanship, a specific physical pain.

clue.text: Definitely not having grill

blocks.note: lacking something means being without it
to grill a suspect is to question them hard

explanation.surface: Someone firmly refuses the offer of a barbecue grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grill' reads as a cooking device, but it is the verb meaning interrogate.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so beyond doubt is an idiom for certainly, an emphatic adverbial phrase of assurance.

clue.text: Piece of news for couple

blocks.note: first meaning: a single report in a newspaper or bulletin
second meaning: two people romantically linked

explanation.surface: A news report about a pair of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A news story is called an item, and a pair seen dating is informally described as an item too.

clue.text: Clear river, catching single rodent

indicators.note: the river catches the following words, holding them within its banks

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
a single thing is one
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A river is cleared after trapping a lone rat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon; it wraps round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame, declaring them free of guilt or accusation.

clue.text: Expression after opening of silver foil?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: first letter of silver
a word is a verbal expression

explanation.surface: Something said when unwrapping silver foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests kitchen wrapping, but it is the light fencing weapon; the question mark flags this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A foil is a type of blade used in fencing, so the general weapon name covers it by example.

clue.text: Payment to keep quality up with electronic withdrawal

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
something kept is held inside, so the payment goes around the rest

blocks.note: merit is a good quality
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A pension payment is maintained while money is withdrawn online.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(TIREM + E)NT: the payment holds the upturned quality plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is withdrawal from working life, and also a withdrawing or retreat in general use.

clue.text: Island suffering harm as navy tired

indicators.note: the words that follow are suffering damage, so their letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An island takes a battering because the navy defending it is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is an island off Cape Cod, Massachusetts, famous as a summer resort.

clue.text: Regret very end of bitter quarrel

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
last letter of bitter
a row (rhyming with cow) is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone deeply regrets how a bitter argument finally ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is grief or deep regret, so the noun matches the feeling of remorse over something done.

clue.text: Politician with line admitted to modest yield

indicators.note: something admitted to a place is let inside it

blocks.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
L is a standard abbreviation for line
coy means shy or modest

explanation.surface: A politician and his party line are welcomed into a humble result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' looks like a noun after 'modest', but it is the verb meaning give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply is to give way and obey a demand, which is what yielding to pressure means.

clue.text: Busy part of year, heading off with self-confidence

indicators.note: removing the heading of a word means its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a month is part of a year
ego is self-esteem or self-confidence

explanation.surface: A confident person sets off busily for part of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go is an idiom for constantly active, rushing about with no rest.

clue.text: Working group going round a province

indicators.note: a group going round something encircles it, holding it inside

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a trio is a group of three
taken as written

explanation.surface: A working party tours a province.
explanation.walkthrough: ON + T(A)RIO: the group of three surrounds the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a Canadian province, home to Toronto and Ottawa, so the general term covers it.

clue.text: Cover evidence without pressure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: proof is evidence
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone hides evidence without being pressed to.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the P from the front of PROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof is the covering on top of a building, so the noun stands for a cover.

clue.text: Control bound to restrict herd is abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters run riot into a new order
restricting something means hemming it in on both sides

blocks.note: a bound is a leap
the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A farmer's fence keeps in a herd that would otherwise be left to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like it describes the herd, but it signals that those letters run wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership means being in charge and directing others, which is to have control.

clue.text: Increase distortion of case with language about love

indicators.note: a distortion twists a word out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
about means around, so the language goes round the next piece

blocks.note: the fodder, as written
Latin is a language
love means zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A legal case is twisted by language about romance and grows bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: The love letter slips inside the language between its last two letters. Love = O comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalation is a rise or intensification, so the noun matches increase used as a noun.

clue.text: Brave humour by labourer carrying stone

indicators.note: someone carrying something holds it within

blocks.note: wit is humour
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A cheerful workman bravely hauls a heavy stone.
explanation.walkthrough: WIT + H(ST)AND: the labourer carries the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave a storm is to face it and hold out against it, exactly what withstand means.

clue.text: Anger in place in complaint

indicators.note: the second in places one thing inside the other

blocks.note: a complaint is an illness or disease
Pl is the abbreviation for Place in addresses

explanation.surface: Fury erupts over a grievance, as though anger has found its place in complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS(PL)EASE. 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or anger them, a verb meaning provoke irritation.

clue.text: Sentimental Greek character, not bold

blocks.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
shy is the opposite of bold

explanation.surface: A soppy, timid Greek person.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushy is informal for soppy or overly emotional, as in a mushy love song.

clue.text: Fruit, not right with a type of cheese

indicators.note: not means the next letter is excluded from the word

blocks.note: a gourd is a fruit of the squash family
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheese board pairs fruit with a certain cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after the town where it was traded.

clue.text: Heartless mob in prison caper

indicators.note: a heartless word has its middle cut out, leaving only its ends
in puts the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
outer letters of mob

explanation.surface: A cruel gang behind bars carries out a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: GA(MB)OL. 'Caper' looks like a crime, but here it means a playful skip.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip and leap about playfully, and to gambol means to frolic in the same way.

clue.text: Renewal of lease isn't necessary

indicators.note: a renewal makes something over again, so these letters are made into a fresh order

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tenant is told that renewing the lease is not required.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, which is what necessary means as an adjective.

clue.text: Weak shell of elegant mollusc

indicators.note: a shell is the outside casing, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: limp means weak or floppy
outer letters of elegant

explanation.surface: A frail, elegant shell from a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' sits naturally beside mollusc, but it is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a sea snail with a conical shell that clings to rocks, a kind of mollusc.

clue.text: Unclear about answer with knowledge left wrongly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: misty means hazy or unclear
A is a standard abbreviation for answer
ken is knowledge, as in beyond my ken
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A vague reply from someone who knows things is left inaccurate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is an old Scots word for knowledge, kept alive in the phrase beyond my ken.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakenly means in error or by mistake, the adverb matching wrongly in sense.

clue.text: Result, guarantee having run out

indicators.note: having something run out means that letter is driven out of the word

blocks.note: to ensure is to guarantee
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A warranty has expired, with consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result' is a verb here, meaning follow as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, which is what result means as a verb.

clue.text: Join in immense amusement

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Taking part in some huge fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of fabric are stitched together, so it is a junction.

clue.text: Impression derived from study over time

blocks.note: a den is a private study or retreat
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A view formed by studying something over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' places the study above time in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a hollow pressed into a surface, a physical impression left by a blow.

clue.text: Engineer elected to cut very large roots

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: OS means outsize, a clothing label for very large
to rig is to engineer an outcome
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: An engineer has been chosen to prune some enormous roots.
explanation.walkthrough: O(RIG IN)S. 'Engineer' is a verb here, meaning fix or fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Origins are where something comes from, its beginnings or source, just as roots are.

clue.text: Maintain mature standard

blocks.note: to aver is to assert or maintain
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Keep to a grown-up level.
explanation.definitionFit: The average is the usual or normal level, so it serves as the norm or benchmark.

clue.text: Bored, having seen tide turn at sea

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and lost, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sailor is bored after watching the tide change while out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninterested feels no curiosity or engagement, the state of being bored.
